items.title: v2.1.332
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[v2.1.332](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.332)** — _Claude Code releases_. — MCP servers can now ship skills (beta), and a new hook event can refuse a skill's inline shell commands.
  - Server skills show as `server:skill` in the / menu
  - Reads on a named pipe nothing writes to now fail after 20 seconds
  - Held messages from other sessions get an Always deliver option
  - Fixed freezes from unbounded hook output and flooding MCP servers

items.title: v2.4.0
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[v2.4.0](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v2.4.0)** — _OpenCode releases_. — OpenCode 2.4.0 gives the desktop app a built-in browser and timer- or cron-driven automations.
  - Imports sign-ins and browsing history from Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari, plus extensions from Chromium stores
  - The agent can read and drive the same pages without switching apps
  - Automations run a prompt, script or shell command on a timer, cron schedule or MCP event
  - The image tool is now `generate_image`; old permission rules map automatically

- 🛠 **[1.0.115](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/releases/tag/v1.0.115)** — _Copilot CLI releases_. — 1.0.115 adds Gemini 4 Hydrogen, GPT-6.2 Astra and MAI-Code-2-Flash to the /model picker.
  - Ctrl+X then A in /model adds and switches to custom provider models in local sessions
  - Structured clarification questions work in ACP editors that support forms
  - Windows sandbox package queries are on by default, with a userPolicy opt-out
  - macOS sandboxed commands can allow specific Mach service lookups

items.title: v1.45.0
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[v1.45.0](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/releases/tag/v1.45.0)** — _OpenHands releases_. — v1.45.0 ships OpenHands Projects in Canvas behind an experimental flag and nests sub-agent conversations under their parent.
  - Project conversations move into the sidebar, with files and PRs beside the chat
  - Factories show their worklogs newest first and can be deleted from their own page
  - Also fixes a range of mobile, accessibility and settings bugs

items.title: Hermes Agent canary canary.20261123T065600Z-v0.23.3
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[Hermes Agent canary canary.20261123T065600Z-v0.23.3](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/tag/canary.20261123T065600Z-v0.23.3)** — _Hermes Agent releases_. — The November 23 Hermes canary build is mostly plugin-catalog additions plus release-pipeline wiring.
  - New catalog entries include beeper-platform, utcp-bridge, valetudo, deny-record and katara memory
  - `stable-release.yml` now wires commit claims in with read-only native legs
  - macOS arm64 DMG and both Windows MSIX builds passed install smoke tests

items.title: Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/24/amazons-decart-acquisition-is-a-bet-on-using-software-to-narrow-the-gap-with-nvidia-in-the-ai-chip-race/)** — _TechCrunch AI_. — Amazon paid a reported $7.5 billion for Decart and wants the software, not the world models.
  - Decart Optimization Stack coaxes more performance out of Amazon's Trainium chips
  - Amazon has worked with Decart on Trainium since 2025
  - Anthropic reportedly tried to buy Decart in the same ballpark
  - Nvidia invested in a $300 million round at a $4 billion valuation

items.title: Anthropic tops 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and expands the protocol for more autonomous AI agents
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Anthropic tops 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and expands the protocol for more autonomous AI agents](https://the-decoder.com/anthropic-tops-700-million-monthly-mcp-sdk-downloads-and-expands-the-protocol-for-more-autonomous-ai-agents/)** — _The Decoder_. — Two years after launch, MCP has passed 700 million monthly SDK downloads and now runs jobs in the background.
  - Tasks runs a long job on a server and reports back when done
  - Elicitation pauses a running process to ask for missing details
  - Skills over MCP, in public beta, load only when needed
  - File uploads for PDFs, spreadsheets and images are rolling out soon

items.title: Elastic puts AI agents to work on the SOC alert backlog
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Elastic puts AI agents to work on the SOC alert backlog](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/24/elastic-security-9-6-features/)** — _Help Net Security AI_. — Elastic Security 9.6 hands the alert backlog to six AlertZero Workers spread across four teams.
  - Workers propose actions with evidence, under Manual, Assisted or Supervised autonomy
  - 143 detection rules cover MCP servers, jailbreaks and stolen API keys
  - Adds Linux ransomware blocking plus custom YARA memory scanning
  - Technical preview in Elastic Cloud Serverless; hosted Enterprise due early December

items.title: We’re launching Humanity’s First Exam and a Kaggle hackathon to test LLM reliability.
items.bullet_md:
- 🔵 **[We’re launching Humanity’s First Exam and a Kaggle hackathon to test LLM reliability.](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/humanitys-first-exam/)** — _Google DeepMind_. — DeepMind's new exam asks whether models get everyday questions right every time, not just once.
  - 544 text and image prompts across 20 foundational capabilities
  - Leaderboard and technical report published with the launch
  - Three-week Kaggle hackathon runs through December 15
  - Prompts were chosen to expose blind spots, not sampled at random

items.title: Google Cloud CISO talks agentic AI security and the future of the SOC
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Google Cloud CISO talks agentic AI security and the future of the SOC](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/24/chris-betz-google-agentic-ai-security/)** — _Help Net Security AI_. — Chris Betz says human reaction time is no longer a viable defense baseline.
  - Attackers now compress six months of reconnaissance into hours
  - The future alert is a verified conclusion, not a raw ticket
  - Juniors move up to doctrine, risk appetite and verifying agent actions
  - Boards should ask if every agent action can be traced and reversed

items.title: Anthropic turns Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop apps for macOS and Windows
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Anthropic turns Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop apps for macOS and Windows](https://the-decoder.com/anthropic-turns-claude-artifacts-into-standalone-desktop-apps-for-macos-and-windows/)** — _The Decoder_. — Anthropic's Artifacts now install as real Mac and Windows apps, turning chat demos into things that live in the dock.
  - Beta as of today, needs the latest Claude desktop app; a free account is enough
  - Installed apps can add menu bar items, transparent windows and notifications
  - Optional full computer access lets them intercept shortcuts and float over other programs

items.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
items.bullet_md:
- 🟢 **[GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities](https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities)** — _OpenAI blog_. — OpenAI's GPT-6 models can now design protein shapes from a prompt and code, matching or beating specialist tools on most tasks.
  - 35 of 322 lab-made minibinders bound their target, a 10.9% hit rate
  - Motif scaffolding reached 43.7% versus 27.8% for RFdiffusion
  - Specialized models still supplied sequences and picked candidates for testing
  - Whole-structure prediction still lags: ESMFold2 averaged a 0.93 TM-score

items.title: Antom 3-in-1 Transformer: A Payment Foundation Model
items.bullet_md:
- 🧪 **[Antom 3-in-1 Transformer: A Payment Foundation Model](https://huggingface.co/papers/2611.25403)** — _HF Daily Papers_. — Ant International put a 7B-parameter foundation model into live card-payment fraud scoring and cut the overall loss rate 37.88% against its XGBoost baseline.
  - One model reads transaction sequences, tabular fields and user graphs
  - Roughly 1.7B of its 7B parameters activate per task route
  - With 25% of the labels it beats training from scratch on all labels

items.title: Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory](https://github.com/ShinMegamiBoson/lookatmyquant)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — A third-party quantiser squeezed Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini into a 5.4 GB build.
  - LookAtMyQuant is MIT-licensed and gives more bits to the parts that matter most
  - The small build beats a larger Unsloth version on GSM8K and HumanEval
  - Runs on an Apple M5 Max, even though the vendor suggests about 20 GB

items.title: v0.34.1rc0: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Add SM100 TP=2 and TP=8 skinny GEMM plans (#69529)
items.bullet_md:
- 🟡 **[v0.34.1rc0: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Add SM100 TP=2 and TP=8 skinny GEMM plans (#69529)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.34.1rc0)** — _vLLM releases_. — Blackwell perf work keeps landing as perf-only tags: this one adds SM100 skinny GEMM plans for Qwen4Exp at tensor parallelism 2 and 8.
  - Same corner as last week's FlashInfer top-k swap, 1.30-2.25x faster long-context decode on GB300
  - Release notes carry the commit and sign-off only, no benchmark figures yet

items.title: Connect AI Agents to Google Workspace: Official MCP Servers & CLI
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Connect AI Agents to Google Workspace: Official MCP Servers & CLI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DO77XGujw_A) — **Google Workspace Developers** (4m33s). — Google's Workspace MCP servers and gwscli CLI are now generally available, wiring agents into Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar and Chat. - Calls are checked against Workspace permissions, DLP rules and classification labels - Google says move agentic access off REST APIs before February 1, 2027 enforcement - Keep is listed as coming soon

items.title: How to Ship Millions of Lines of Agent-Written Code — Jarred Sumner, Anthropic
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [How to Ship Millions of Lines of Agent-Written Code — Jarred Sumner, Anthropic](https://youtube.com/watch?v=TvsF67C2F54) — **AI Engineer** (22m30s). — Bun landed a several-million-line AOT compiler PR, rewritten five times in a month, at 4x less memory and 2x faster startup. - Tests that predate the project are what make agent-written code trustworthy - Kept Claude Code in TypeScript instead of porting its tests to Rust - Test262 and the existing Bun and WebKit tests back the compiler

items.title: Build the Workshop Before the Software Factory — Armin Ronacher, Earendil
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Build the Workshop Before the Software Factory — Armin Ronacher, Earendil](https://youtube.com/watch?v=JNexz3Tbiu8) — **AI Engineer** (19m56s). — Human attention, not model capability, is the limit: build the workshop before the software factory. - Pi's core tools are unchanged after a year; the models got better - Tasks now run 14 minutes instead of two and a half - 141 projects started, only 10 to 15 kept alive - Executive summaries instead of reading code

items.title: Shadcn Just Rebuilt UI for AI Agents (UI SDK)
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Shadcn Just Rebuilt UI for AI Agents (UI SDK)](https://youtube.com/watch?v=ubK6Q53jKg8) — **Better Stack** (9m01s). — Vercel and shadcn's UI SDK lets agents act on a component's state instead of screenshotting and clicking through pages. - createAgent exposes snapshot, act and query from the framework package - In one F1 app test the browser agent made five calls, the bridge agent three - The browser agent read about 10 times more text

items.title: AI Writes 44% More Code. So Why Isn't More Software Shipping?
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [AI Writes 44% More Code. So Why Isn't More Software Shipping?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cI1WVdTpFZY) — **DopeShit** (9m12s). — Harvard tracked 720,542 workers at 655 companies: 44% more code written, only ~14% more finished work. - Time to merge rose 56% and review comments rose 39% - Letting AI review the code has not fixed the review line - The same pattern appears in hospitals with AI scribes - Two simulated futures for 2031, and what they mean for developers

items.title: My AI Coding Agent Broke a Rule, Then Rewrote CLAUDE.md
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [My AI Coding Agent Broke a Rule, Then Rewrote CLAUDE.md](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DGw2ObWdP1c) — **Sebastian Buzdugan** (9m25s). — Candid, sponsor-funded test of whether a rules service actually stops agents bending instruction files. - Qodo turned instruction files across 13 repos into 361 structured rules - Hand audit of 69 rules: 50 faithful, 8 over-hardened, 6 misread - Get Rules prevented one of 8 rule-break attempts; each task ran once - Imported rules also blocked one valid fix and overrode one request

items.title: Securing AI Agents | Mariane Bekker (1Password) | All Day AI 2026
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Securing AI Agents | Mariane Bekker (1Password) | All Day AI 2026](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S6NhGp5GFaQ) — **Anaconda, Inc.** (19m41s). — For anyone about to hand an agent real API keys: where credentials leak, and how a vault hands them over at runtime. - Covers identity, authentication, secrets management and permissions for agents - Secrets stay in the vault and reach agents and scripts at runtime

items.title: I Beat Jev AI with a Fine-Tuned Open-Source Model
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [I Beat Jev AI with a Fine-Tuned Open-Source Model](https://youtube.com/watch?v=YNal-nlQ5F8) — **James Briggs** (33m16s). — A 436M-parameter local model beats Jev on routing accuracy, calibration, latency and cost in one workspace. - Picks the right agent on 85.9% of 205 test posts against Jev's 78.0% - Calibration error 0.052 versus 0.071, at ~27 ms per decision on an RTX 5000 Ada - Under 0.1¢ per 1K decisions on an M4 Max against Jev's 5¢

items.title: MCP Registry: The App Store for AI Agent Tools
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [MCP Registry: The App Store for AI Agent Tools](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Er0ay2ecHw8) — **Kernel Cast** (2m15s). — For anyone new to MCP: a 2m15s map of the registry agents query to find tool servers. - Entries are `server.json` records pointing at npm, PyPI or OCI packages, or remote URLs - Framed as an App Store for agent tools, spanning GitHub, databases and search

items.title: [AINews] Gemini 4 Neon marks GDM's full return as a Frontier Lab
items.bullet_md: - 📰 **[[AINews] Gemini 4 Neon marks GDM's full return as a Frontier Lab](https://latent.space/p/ainews-gemini-4-neon-marks-gdm-s-full-return-as-a-frontier-lab/)** — _Latent Space (swyx)_. — Gemini 4 Neon beats Astra and Fable on LiveBench, cuts the TS Rust benchmark runtime by 48.6%, and ranks #3 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index at 61.

items.title: ExecuTorch-TensorRT: PyTorch Robot Policies at NVIDIA TensorRT Speed
items.bullet_md:
- 📝 **[ExecuTorch-TensorRT: PyTorch Robot Policies at NVIDIA TensorRT Speed](https://pytorch.org/blog/executorch-tensorrt-pytorch-robot-policies-at-nvidia-tensorrt-speed/)** — _PyTorch blog_. — NVIDIA and Meta ship ExecuTorch-TensorRT, which runs TensorRT-compiled PyTorch robot policies without libtorch.
  - Within 4% of ONNX-TensorRT on a Jetson Orin Nano, in speed and memory
  - pi0.5 (3.6B) makes an action chunk in 467 ms where eager mode runs out of memory
  - Robot install drops to about 4.6 GB instead of 11 GB

items.title: Armin Ronacher and Mario Zechner on Coding With Agents
items.bullet_md: - 📝 **[Armin Ronacher and Mario Zechner on Coding With Agents](https://www.aihero.dev/armin-ronacher-and-mario-zechner-on-coding-with-agents~fn8vd)** — _AI Hero (Matt Pocock)_. — Mario Zechner tells Matt Pocock that agent verification is overrated, since agents measure the wrong thing and still cannot do system design.

items.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
items.bullet_md:
- 🟢 **[Perplexity and Intelligence](https://openai.com/index/perplexity-and-intelligence)** — _OpenAI blog_. — Jakub Pachocki argues perplexity should be the shared cross-lab yardstick, and proposes common limits labs commit not to cross.
  - OpenAI published numbers on a fixed internal-code set: GPT-3.5 ~0.99, GPT-4 ~0.91
  - Capabilities emerged below 0.8, with math breakthroughs at ~0.76
  - He expects the next transformative window around 0.68-0.7 log-perplexity

items.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
items.bullet_md:
- 🧪 **[Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention](https://huggingface.co/papers/2611.30634)** — _HF Daily Papers_. — LoomFormer's loom attention lets a Transformer rewire its circuits per token, matching models trained with over 3x the compute.
  - Vertical attention over earlier heads runs through a per-token matrix memory, a second residual stream
  - Costs 2% extra FLOPs; LoomPythia-2.8B matches Pythia-12B at 0-shot and beats it at 5-shot

items.title: Show HN: I built a game where you are an LLM's subagent
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Show HN: I built a game where you are an LLM's subagent](https://github.com/gulivan/worker755)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — A browser game that flips the agent loop: a real LLM manager hands you shell tasks on a 90-second clock, then writes your performance review.
  - The manager can be Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM or Kimi, or a local Ollama server
  - Each mission has a hidden ground-truth check, scoring the times it signed off on broken work

items.title: Anthropic a public beta of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, letting businesses keep Claude data in their own cloud while…
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Anthropic a public beta of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, letting businesses keep Claude data in their own cloud while…](https://claude.com/resources/articles/zero-data-retention-with-enterprise-frontier-safeguards?_bhlid=05c5ba9f186c7355164698509156b6e3823c03fb)** — _The Rundown AI · Nov 24_. — Anthropic opened Enterprise Frontier Safeguards to public beta, adding cross-request misuse monitoring without retaining customer data.
  - Customers bring their own S3 or Google Cloud Storage; neither Anthropic nor the cloud provider keeps a copy
  - A flagged risk creates a Safety Case with case ID and harm category, but no inputs or outputs
  - Live on Claude Platform, AWS, Bedrock and Google Cloud; Microsoft Foundry coming soon
